author: WP08
summary: Audits the EasyGL family's bug history and semantics (MRT, base vertex, occlusion, wireframe, fog, colour masks, targets, SpriteBatch index ceiling, back buffer, recovery, viewport, stencil, buffer shadows, clears, tests, Xvfb and oracle evidence) and contrasts OPENGL4 and PORTABLEGL. Much is stale at 009d40f5: base vertex, index wrap, clear depth bit, wireframe design, cube and volume formats, SetDataRaw readback and OPENGL4's dispatch all changed. The site had thorough EasyGL and OpenGL4 internals but not these semantics; two EasyGL deep dives now carry them.

concepts.section: OpenGL II: Programmable, Web, and Portable Profiles
concepts.text: Five public profiles share CNA's internal EasyGL implementation and the sibling easy-gl project; Linux defaults to OPENGLES3, Emscripten to WEBGL2, and EASYGL is not a selector.
tokens: It is no longer a value you can pass to CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER

concepts.section: OpenGL II: Programmable, Web, and Portable Profiles
concepts.text: The independent OPENGL4 and CPU-only PORTABLEGL implementations are distinct from the shared EasyGL path and must be reasoned about separately.
tokens: OPENGL4 and PORTABLEGL are not EasyGL

concepts.text: CNA's docs/easygl_bugs.md carries its own staleness banner: written before thousands of lines of later EasyGL changes, few rows re-confirmed, the rest spot-checked; treat it as methodology, not a current defect list.
CNA's docs/rendertarget-support.md likewise predates render-target implementations that later code closed.

concepts.section: Confirmed fixed since the original bug list
concepts.text: Anisotropic filtering forwards the requested MaxAnisotropy (XNA's unsigned conversion, clamped to the device cap) when GL_EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic is advertised, through sampler objects or a texture parameter on ES 2.0.

concepts.section: Confirmed fixed since the original bug list
concepts.text: Cube render targets take a real depthFormat parameter instead of a hard-coded always-has-depth flag, and each face of a multisampled cube owns its own multisample colour renderbuffer.
The old MRT leak diagnosis is not current: EasyGL owns one reusable MRT framebuffer, calls FinalizeCurrentMRT() before every destination change and installs a validated ordered set.
EasyGL_MRT_TwoAttachments now runs a one-to-four-output ShaderEffect contract covering set replacement, per-target masks, MSAA resolve, usage, readback and immediate sampling.

The historical two-attachment MRT failure expected an old value to survive a DiscardContents bind through single-output BasicEffect, so it could not tell an inactive attachment from a single-output shader.
An upstream easy-gl GL-state-desynchronisation failure in that sibling's own resource smoke test is evidence about the sibling project, not a CNA defect.

target.evidence: sibling easy-gl repository (not pinned by CNA); no such registration in CNA's CMake

concepts.note: Kept generically: sibling-project test failures are not renderer evidence.

concepts.text: On the ES 3.0 path a nonzero base vertex formerly reached glDrawElementsBaseVertex unchecked, a process-failure risk because meta-gl terminates on a missing entry point.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: RequiresBaseVertexPointerRebase is true for every profile except OpenGL33, so OPENGLES3 rebases attribute pointers instead of calling glDrawElementsBaseVertex; the page states the current rule.

concepts.text: Every profile except OPENGL33 satisfies a nonzero base vertex by shifting enabled attribute pointers and restoring them after the draw; a negative base vertex is folded into a rewritten index slice.

OcclusionQuery::PixelCount is 0 or 1 only where GL_ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED is used (ES 3.0/WebGL 2); EasyGL probes GL_SAMPLES_PASSED once per process and keeps the exact count where the driver accepts it, and PixelCountIsPreciseEXT reports which.

Wireframe uses a real polygon mode (glPolygonMode, GL_NV_polygon_mode, WEBGL_polygon_mode) and SupportsCapability(WireFrame) is true exactly when one exists; otherwise the draw is refused rather than re-expanded to GL_LINES.
concepts.note: Older text said EasyGL re-expanded triangles to GL_LINES and needed no polygon mode; the page states the current design.

concepts.text: Stock-effect fog is computed from FNA's CPU-prepared view-space fog vector as 1 - saturate(dot(position, fogVector)).
Bare DrawColoredPrimitives callbacks receive matrices but no GpuDrawParams by contract; EasyGL's effect-aware stock path is its Draw*PrimitivesEx route.
ApplyBlendState stores all four ColorWriteChannels; slot 0 goes through glColorMask and indexed-mask profiles submit each MRT slot; profiles without indexed masks refuse unequal active masks.
Because GL clears respect the colour mask and XNA clears do not, each EasyGL clear temporarily enables all channels and restores the requested masks.

The renderer-level preserveContents factory flag is deliberately unused: an FBO bind never touches attachments, so every target preserves and the shared device clears exact DiscardContents on each real bind; Preserve and Platform behave identically.
concepts.note: A design decision at 009d40f5, not a missing feature.

concepts.text: Ordinary Texture2D uploads accept explicit mip levels but never regenerate from level 0; render-target unbind generates the chain.
Texture3D and TextureCube no longer ignore the requested SurfaceFormat: ClassifyTextureCubeFormatEXT and ClassifyTexture3DFormatEXT store real formats per profile and refuse unsupported ones.
TextureCube now joins EasyGL's context-loss recovery registry; Texture3D still does not (EasyGLTexture3DRenderer is not a recoverable resource).
EasyGLEffectRenderer::Unbind() is deliberately empty; the next bind or SpriteBatch flush installs its own program.
The SpriteBatch 16-bit index wrap past 16,384 quads is fixed: EasyGL chunks at XNA's 2,048-sprite submission size (kMaxSpritesPerBatch).
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the draw path flushes when pending vertices reach kMaxSpritesPerBatch*4 and continues the batch; the page keeps the arithmetic as a labelled historical case.

concepts.text: VertexBuffer/IndexBuffer GetData have no GPU readback on any renderer; they answer from CPU shadows (corrected fully in the GetData section).
tokens: the CPU shadow is the readback

concepts.text: Forwarding a real non-Color SurfaceFormat to the GPU was once formally blocked by a Color-only Texture::ValidateFormat contract; at 009d40f5 families classify formats (ClassifySurfaceFormatEXT) and EasyGL stores real formats.
concepts.note: The blocking decision no longer holds; current format support is documented on the renderer and EasyGL internals pages (ClassifySurfaceFormatEXT, 'no classifier means Color only').

concepts.text: The EasyGL factory now receives the requested depth format and UpdatePresentationFormatEXT applies later changes; the multisample back-buffer framebuffer follows DepthFormat including stencil, colour stays RGBA8.
concepts.note: Older text: the factory dropped the three presentation fields and the MSAA FBO lacked stencil.

concepts.text: EasyGL_DepthFormat cycles all four DepthFormat values through the manager and SetPresentationParameters and checks storage and survival.
The stencil test is enabled only while the active target or back buffer has a Depth24Stencil8 plane.
tokens: only while the active target or back buffer really has

concepts.text: Disabling context recovery after construction and before content loading enables Texture2D CPU-shadow discard and stops new GL resources joining EasyGL's recovery registry; existing resources stay registered and re-enabling reconstructs nothing.
On desktop either debug key performs a complete synchronous loss-and-restore cycle; in a browser F9 requests loss and F10 restore asynchronously through WebGL events.
The 16-bit ceiling is computable: 65,536 indices / 4 vertices per quad = 16,384 quads, and the 16,385th sprite wrapped its base index to zero and redrew the first sprite.
Lesson for any renderer that narrows an index type: compute the ceiling and test exactly at and one past it rather than assuming it is large enough.
tokens: test exactly at and one past it

concepts.text: The old mitigation advice (split batches, use atlases to stay under the ceiling) is unnecessary at 009d40f5 because the renderer chunks transparently.
tokens: unbounded from the caller's point of view

concepts.text: A one-off run of EasyGL against the real-XNA references in the 31-scene era matched 10 of 31 scenes exactly (CNA's own divergence report).
concepts.note: Dated CNA prose; the corpus has 39 scenes at 009d40f5 and later figures are on the verification section.

concepts.text: It was not made a permanent gate because EasyGL on Mesa versus DXVK-produced references mixes driver differences with rendering differences, unlike the DIRECTX9 comparison through one DXVK stack.

concepts.text: Divergences split into seventeen silhouette-edge rasterisation-convention differences, two imperceptible rounding differences and two real defects (negative FogEnd rendered black; per-vertex Fresnel not interpolated like XNA).

The fog-gradient and Fresnel findings are addressed in the shared stock shaders (FNA fog vector; per-vertex Fresnel as in XNA's EnvironmentMapEffect) for every stock variant; the named scenes were not re-measured here.
tokens: Fresnel scalar is evaluated per vertex
concepts.note: The fix now lives in the shared corpus used by EasyGL and OPENGL4.

concepts.text: A closed-form fog expression written directly in FogStart/FogEnd terms is not what the shader computes; fog comes from the CPU-prepared vector.
tokens: is not what the shader computes

concepts.text: CNA's docs/d3d9-divergence-report.md still records the EasyGL fog and Fresnel findings as open; the document is historical for those rows.
concepts.note: Documentation staleness inside CNA; the current shader behaviour is recorded on the pages above.

concepts.text: SetViewport programs the GL viewport and depth range immediately for the back buffer, 2D targets and cube faces, flipping Y against the active target height.
tokens: programs the GL viewport and depth range immediately

concepts.text: EasyGL's SpriteBatch keeps a custom sub-viewport and projects from its logical size, comparing against the presentation rectangle so a letterboxed default viewport is not mistaken for a game-set one.
tokens: not mistaken for a game-set one

concepts.text: Viewport tests: EasyGL_ViewportState and EasyGL_Viewport_Subregion.

EasyGL applies viewport state at the call site, a broader scope than a deferred renderer that must capture per-draw state; Vulkan now captures viewport per deferred draw, so the old back-buffer-only limitation is gone.
ApplyRasterizerState controls scissor enable and SetScissorRect flips Y against the active target height; EasyGL_Scissor compares disabled, enabled and disabled-again pixels.

concepts.section: A claim this chapter itself got wrong: two-sided stencil's shared mask is correct, not a bug
concepts.text: ApplyDepthStencilState passes the same stencilMask to both faces, which is correct: XNA 4.0 has separate clockwise and counter-clockwise functions and operations but one StencilMask and one StencilWriteMask.

concepts.section: A claim this chapter itself got wrong: two-sided stencil's shared mask is correct, not a bug
concepts.text: The counter-clockwise operation tuple reaches a separate set_stencil_op_separate call; with GL's CCW front faces XNA's counter-clockwise tuple goes to GL_FRONT and the clockwise tuple to GL_BACK.
tokens: XNA's counter-clockwise tuple belongs to GL's front face
concepts.note: An older excerpt showed the clockwise tuple on the front face; the current mapping is the reverse.

concepts.text: SetReferenceStencil re-issues the stencil function with the remembered function and mask so ReferenceStencil applies independently of a new DepthStencilState.

VertexBuffer and IndexBuffer GetData return bytes from the resource-level cpuShadow_ on every renderer, which preserves XNA's SetData-then-GetData contract because XNA has no GPU write path into these buffers.
tokens: no GPU write path into these buffers

concepts.text: WriteOnly buffers make GetData throw NotSupportedException, but the shadow is still maintained because whole-buffer submission needs it.
tokens: Write-only buffers still keep a shadow
concepts.note: Older text said write-only bypasses the shadow.

concepts.text: The options-taking dynamic SetData wrappers now refresh the shadow; the stale-shadow defect is absent at 009d40f5.
tokens: The options overloads refresh the shadow

concepts.text: SetDataRaw now goes through the same validated upload routine and CPU shadow, and GetDataRawEXT reads custom-layout bytes back; SetDataRawAtEXT writes a window of the buffer.
concepts.note: Older text: SetDataRaw bypassed the shadow and no raw readback existed; the page states the current API.

concepts.section: Clear is immediate GL state, but Target is not colour-only
concepts.text: The seven EasyGL clear methods are immediate glClear paths, and the depth and stencil variants force full depth and stencil write masks.
tokens: force full depth and stencil write masks

concepts.section: Clear is immediate GL state, but Target is not colour-only
concepts.text: EasyGL now disables the scissor test for every clear and restores it, because an XNA clear covers the complete target while GL honours an enabled scissor.
tokens: disables the scissor test for the clear
concepts.note: Older text said a clear could cover less than the target because of the scissor.

concepts.section: Clear is immediate GL state, but Target is not colour-only
concepts.text: The colour-only Clear hook requested Colour|Depth without forcing the depth mask, so a Target-only clear could clear or keep depth depending on prior state; fixed by REMED-GFX-142.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: EasyGLRenderer::Clear is colour only at 009d40f5 and is what GraphicsDevice routes a bare ClearOptions::Target and the raw-float overload to; EasyGL_ClearOverloads exercises the overloads. Described on the EasyGL page as a historical note.

concepts.section: Clear is immediate GL state, but Target is not colour-only
concepts.text: Clear-overload tests verify resulting colour and that a depth-only clear preserves colour; a complete selectivity test must also prime and check depth around a target-only clear.
Do not carry an old fixed count of EasyGL failures forward; registrations change with configuration and fixtures get replaced.

EasyGL_GraphicsDevice_ReferenceStencil is still annotated as a documented known failure in CMake while EasyGLRenderer::SetReferenceStencil now applies the reference independently; its current pass state was not established.
Networking and audio failures in large corpora are environment classes, not renderer evidence; a baseline needs commit, registrations, display/driver and filter.
EasyGL needs a window and GL context, so a native screenshot needs a display server (Xvfb with Mesa llvmpipe), unlike display-free SOFTWARE screenshots.

The ad-hoc, unregistered cna_xvfb_screenshot_demo_easygl builds examples/xvfb_screenshot_demo.cpp and saves via the examples helper SaveBackBufferScreenshotEXT; the registered rotation pixel test is EasyGL_SpriteBatch_Rotation_Golden.

concepts.section: OPENGL4: modern core without the EasyGL family
concepts.text: OPENGL4 is an independent family with its own loader against system GL and a verified 4.1 core context; OPENGL33 and OPENGL4 are not two settings of one renderer.
tokens: OPENGL4 is not a sixth EasyGL profile

concepts.section: OPENGL4: modern core without the EasyGL family
concepts.text: OPENGL4 targets GLSL 410 core by adapting the shared GLSL ES 3.00 stock corpus, so its shader path is shared with EasyGL at 009d40f5, contrary to older text.
tokens: share two things with EasyGL on purpose

concepts.section: OPENGL4: modern core without the EasyGL family
concepts.text: EasyGL carries ES and Web workarounds while OPENGL4 assumes a modern desktop core; a context or loader bug in one is not evidence about the other, but a shared stock-shader change must be tested on both.

concepts.section: OPENGL4: modern core without the EasyGL family
concepts.text: OPENGL4 owns real 2D targets, MRT and occlusion queries.

concepts.section: OPENGL4: modern core without the EasyGL family
concepts.text: OPENGL4 has no stride-driven BindProgramForStride with a coloured tail at 009d40f5: SelectProgram chooses from effect state and an unmatched declaration is refused by RequireDeclarationFitsStockProgram.
concepts.note: The hybrid colored-tail dispatch belongs to the pre-rewrite renderer; the page states the current design.

concepts.section: OPENGL4: modern core without the EasyGL family
concepts.text: For selection and triage treat OPENGL33 as an EasyGL profile and OPENGL4 as a separate family; names encode neither shared code nor an upgrade path.
tokens: neither shared code nor an upgrade path

concepts.section: PORTABLEGL: OpenGL-shaped software, not a GPU driver
concepts.text: PORTABLEGL runs a pinned PortableGL revision's OpenGL 3.x-shaped pipeline on the CPU; its shaders are C vertex and fragment callbacks registered with pglCreateProgram and it creates no GPU resource.
tokens: creates no GPU resource of any kind

concepts.section: PORTABLEGL: OpenGL-shaped software, not a GPU driver
concepts.text: Implemented scope: unlit coloured (stride 16) and textured (stride 20) BasicEffect, a textured SpriteBatch, and real blend, depth-stencil, rasterizer, viewport and scissor state.

concepts.section: PORTABLEGL: OpenGL-shaped software, not a GPU driver
concepts.text: Render targets, MRT, cube and volume textures, occlusion queries, custom effects, MSAA, anisotropy and mip mapping are not implemented; lighting, fog, alpha test, skinning, instancing and multi-stream are refused deterministically, not emulated slowly.

concepts.section: PORTABLEGL: OpenGL-shaped software, not a GPU driver
concepts.text: PortableGL is useful for deterministic device-free experiments but is not a substitute for EasyGL conformance evidence; pixel agreement compares two independent rasterisers.
tokens: not a substitute for EasyGL conformance evidence

concepts.text: Decision map: ES 2.0/WebGL 1 -> OPENGLES2/WEBGL1 (narrow ceilings); ES 3/WebGL 2 -> OPENGLES3/WEBGL2; desktop EasyGL -> OPENGL33; desktop core -> OPENGL4; CPU GL-shaped -> PORTABLEGL.
OPENGLES3 and WEBGL2 do not share one internal profile path: they are distinct GlProfile values and WebGL 2 lacks indexed colour masks, compute and indirect draw.
concepts.note: Older table said the two names share one internal profile path.

issues.text: EasyGL volume textures are not registered with the GL context-loss recovery registry (EasyGLTexture3DRenderer is not a RecoverableResource), so Texture3D content is lost after a real WebGL context loss; cube textures are registered.

EasyGL_GraphicsDevice_ReferenceStencil is still annotated in CMake as a documented known failure while EasyGLRenderer::SetReferenceStencil now re-issues the stencil function; whether the test passes at 009d40f5 is not established.
On OpenGL ES 3.0 and WebGL 2 contexts OcclusionQuery::PixelCount() is boolean (0 or 1) because only GL_ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED exists; PixelCountIsPreciseEXT() reports it.
Former defect: OPENGLES3 reached glDrawElementsBaseVertex for a nonzero base vertex without an ES 3.2 check; at 009d40f5 every profile except OPENGL33 rebases attribute pointers.
Former defect: EasyGL SpriteBatch wrapped its uint16 index base at the 16,385th quad of one batch; at 009d40f5 it flushes every 2,048 sprites (kMaxSpritesPerBatch).
Former defect: EasyGL's colour-only Clear hook added the depth bit (REMED-GFX-142); at 009d40f5 it clears colour only and neutralises scissor and colour masks for the clear.

CNA's docs/d3d9-divergence-report.md still records the EasyGL negative-FogEnd and Fresnel findings as open although the shared stock shaders now implement FNA's fog vector and per-vertex Fresnel; the two scenes were not re-measured.
The WebGL identities (WEBGL1, WEBGL2) have no native test registrations; browser behaviour (context loss, presentation, host-owned loop) needs a separate browser run.
